issues.failure_explanation: Definition 2.4 requires eq-discrete-SLDG to hold for every test function in H_0(Omega_K), an infinite-dimensional L^2 space, whereas the CSLDG/SLDG method actually computed (Section 2.2 and Section 4) determines P-th order DG polynomials by testing only against the P+1 basis functions per element. Under the change of variables y = Phi(x) (characteristic flow from t_n to t_{n+1}), eq-discrete-SLDG is equivalent to U^{n+1}_K(y) = U^n_h(Phi^{-1}(y))|det DPhi^{-1}(y)| a.e. on Omega_K, i.e. the scheme is the exact conservative remap (the exact solution operator of the PDE) restricted to Omega: it involves no spatial discretization and its solutions are generic L^2 functions, not polynomials. What the paper establishes is therefore L^2 well-posedness of exact evolution, while the abstract/intro/conclusion claim that the existence, uniqueness and stability of the CSLDG numerical solutions/scheme are established (for the first time), and the theorems characterize eq-discrete-SLDG as 'the fully discrete scheme'.

failure_location.quote: First, the existence and uniqueness of the CSLDG numerical solutions are proven, along with the stability of the numerical scheme.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Definition 2.4 and Theorems 3.7-3.9 for the per-element polynomial test/solution space actually used (existence/uniqueness then follow from finite-dimensional linear algebra, and the stability/uniqueness argument transfers because the difference of two polynomial solutions is an admissible test), or explicitly re-scope all claims to the idealized scheme of Definition 2.4, acknowledging that it coincides with exact evolution.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's headline theoretical-contribution claims (abstract, introduction, theorem characterizations, conclusion) are unreliable as statements about the CSLDG/SLDG method: the discretizations actually described (Section 2.2) and implemented (Sections 4-5) are not covered by Theorems 3.7-3.9.
issues.title: Advertised existence/uniqueness/stability results analyze an exact-evolution idealization, not the CSLDG scheme
issues.why_classification: A supported resolution with contained work exists (the polynomial scheme is easily shown well-posed and the paper's own stability technique transfers to it), so a recognizably comparable result survives; but as written the central claims assert coverage of a numerical scheme that the proofs never analyze, which is more than a local slip.

issues.failure_explanation: Both lemmas assert exact L^P-norm invariance of the adjoint solution under the characteristic flow. Both proofs perform the change of variables x* -> x* + int A(s(tau),tau) dtau as if it were a rigid translation: Lemma 3.2 claims the integration domain is unchanged, Lemma 3.3 claims dx = dx* because the integral 'is a constant'. The integral depends on the base point x* through the characteristic s(tau), and the flow map's Jacobian is exp(int div A dtau), which differs from 1 in general; only C^1 smoothness of A is assumed, not div A = 0. Counterexample (d = 1, A(x) = -x): psi(x,t_1) = Psi(x e^{-(t_2-t_1)}), so ||psi(.,t_1)||_{L^P(R)} = e^{(t_2-t_1)/P}||Psi||_{L^P(R)} != ||Psi||, and analogously ||psi(.,t_1)||_{L^P(tilde-Omega^{t_1})} = e^{(t_2-t_1)/P}||Psi||_{L^P(tilde-Omega^{t_2})} for Lemma 3.3. (Lemma 3.2's proof also asserts H_0(Omega) is contained in L^P for all P < infinity, which fails for P > 2.) The false equality is invoked in Lemma 3.4's boundedness step and in Theorem 3.8's proof, so those proofs and Theorems 3.7 and 3.9, which rely on them, are unproven as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact invariance by two-sided norm bounds carrying the flow-Jacobian factor (|det DPhi| bounded above and below on the relevant compact sets), and rerun the proofs of Lemma 3.4 and Theorems 3.7-3.9 with these inequalities; all stated conclusions survive.
issues.overall_effect: Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3 are false for any field with div A not identically 0; the boundedness proof of Lemma 3.4 and the existence/stability/uniqueness proofs of Theorems 3.7-3.9 fail as written, although their stated conclusions remain true after repair (their constants are allowed to depend on (T, dt, Omega, A)).
issues.title: Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3 falsely assert L^P-norm invariance: characteristic flow treated as a unit-Jacobian translation
issues.why_classification: The two lemmas are false as stated and the repair requires a genuine change-of-variables argument with flow-Jacobian bounds rather than a typo-level fix, but no downstream statement, regime, or rate is lost because the theorems already allow constants depending on A.

issues.failure_explanation: H_0(Omega) is defined with supp compactly contained in Omega. (i) The claim that it 'becomes a Hilbert space' is false: it is a union of closed subspaces over compact subsets and is not complete (cutoffs of 1 on (0,1) with supports in [1/n, 1-1/n] converge in L^2 to a function not compactly supported in (0,1)). (ii) The paper simultaneously asserts supp{U^n_i} = Omega_i and U^n_i in H_0(Omega_i); a function whose support equals the closed element is not compactly contained in it, so the inference 'Since supp{U^n_i} = Omega_i, it further follows that U^n_i in H_0(Omega_i)' is invalid. (iii) Theorem 3.7 constructs U^1_K = W^1_K * chi_{Omega_K} and claims membership in H_0(Omega_K), concluding U^n_h in H_0(Omega); but the scheme's solution is the exact remap whose essential support generically reaches the outflow boundary (1D: A = 1, Omega = (0,1), U_0 supported in (0.1, 0.9), dt = 0.2 gives supp U^1_h = [0.3, 1]), so the stated conclusion is false as written. The same membership is invoked to justify the test-function choices in Theorems 3.8 and 3.9.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine H_0(Omega) as {f in L^2(R^d) : supp f contained in the closure of Omega} (a closed, hence complete, subspace), or phrase all elementwise statements in L^2 with zero extension; the support bookkeeping and all proofs then go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The Hilbert-space claim, the conclusions of Propositions 3.6-3.7, the construction step and conclusion of Theorem 3.7, and the test-admissibility steps in Theorems 3.8-3.9 are false or unjustified under the paper's own definition of H_0.
issues.title: Defective H_0 framework: non-Hilbert space and compact-support membership claims incompatible with supp = element
issues.why_classification: A one-line redefinition restores consistency and completeness, and every method, conclusion, rate, and advertised scope survives.

issues.failure_explanation: Section 4.1 writes the split equation as U_t = L_xy U with L_xy = a*partial_x + b*partial_y. For the paper's conservative transport equation U_t + partial_x(aU) + partial_y(bU) = 0, the generator is L_xy = -partial_x(a*) - partial_y(b*); the displayed operator has both the wrong sign and the non-conservative form, and it contradicts the paper's own splitting stages, which evolve u_t + (au)_x = 0 and u_t + (bu)_y = 0. The correction is not a single forced character change: a conservative and a non-conservative repair are mathematically different for variable coefficients, and the correct choice must be reconstructed from the stage equations.
